title: Final Test
blurb: Assesses the whole B2 level · Lessons 1–48

steps.html:
Sixty questions across all twelve chapters — five from each. This is the assessment for the level as a whole, not for the last unit. There is no time limit and you can retake it.

  • 60 questions · pass mark 70%
  • Five questions from every chapter
  • Every grammar point in the level
  • Vocabulary and function across all twelve wordlists

steps.title: Chapter 1
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: What did happen at the meeting?
What did happened at the meeting?
steps.why: What is the subject here, so no auxiliary is used.

steps.title: Chapter 1
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Make it indirect: 'How much does it cost?'
options: Do you know how much does it cost?
Do you know how much it costs?
Do you know how much costs it?
steps.answer: Do you know how much it costs?
steps.why: Statement order, and the auxiliary disappears.

steps.title: Chapter 1
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'She ___ for the same firm since she left university.'
steps.why: Since + a point in time, with the present perfect.

steps.title: Chapter 1
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: You need to end a long call politely. Which is best?
options: I'd better let you go — I've got a meeting shortly.
You've been talking for a long time.
steps.answer: I'd better let you go — I've got a meeting shortly.
steps.why: It puts the pressure on the speaker's own schedule, not on the other person.

steps.title: Chapter 1
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: To accidentally say something embarrassing is to …
steps.why: Put your foot in it.

steps.title: Chapter 2
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: The office is dark and the door is locked. Which is the strongest deduction?
steps.why: Must for near-certainty drawn from evidence.

steps.title: Chapter 2
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: She might not have seen us.
steps.why: Negative deduction uses can't have.

steps.title: Chapter 2
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'The decision resulted ___ a sharp fall in applications.'
steps.why: Result in a consequence; result from a cause.

steps.title: Chapter 2
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Illogical uses the prefix il- because …
options: the stem begins with an l
steps.answer: the stem begins with an l
steps.why: il- before l, im- before m or p, ir- before r.

steps.title: Chapter 2
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which agrees most strongly?
options: That's one way of looking at it.
steps.why: Maximum agreement, despite the negative form.

steps.title: Chapter 3
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'We ___ the border when the engine ___ .'
steps.why: Continuous for the longer action, simple for the interruption.

steps.title: Chapter 3
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'By the time we arrived, the course ___ .'
steps.why: Past perfect for what was finished before that past point.

steps.title: Chapter 3
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which answers how long?
options: She had waited at the station.
She had been waiting at the station for three hours.
steps.answer: She had been waiting at the station for three hours.
steps.why: Past perfect continuous measures the period before a past moment.

steps.title: Chapter 3
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: An American speaker's fall and vacation are a British speaker's …
steps.why: Same things, different variety.

steps.title: Chapter 3
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: To go somewhere that makes you uneasy because it is unfamiliar is to step …
steps.why: Out of your comfort zone.

steps.title: Chapter 4
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which says the speaker has more than one brother?
options: My brother, who lives in Astana, is an engineer.
My brother who lives in Astana is an engineer.
steps.answer: My brother who lives in Astana is an engineer.
steps.why: No commas means the clause identifies which brother.

steps.title: Chapter 4
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which relative pronoun can be omitted?
options: The woman who called is waiting.
The report which I sent is out of date.
The report, which took a week, is out of date.
steps.answer: The report which I sent is out of date.
steps.why: Only when the pronoun is the object of its clause.

steps.title: Chapter 4
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: '___ of the residents share a kitchen.'
steps.why: Most of the + a defined group.

steps.title: Chapter 4
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: When rising rents push long-standing residents out of an area, the area is being …
steps.why: Gentrified.

steps.title: Chapter 4
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Fluent speech is hard to follow mainly because …
steps.why: The difficulty is where one word ends and the next begins.

steps.title: Chapter 5
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: It is already arranged with your manager. Which is best?
options: I start on Monday every week.
steps.why: Present continuous for a fixed arrangement.

steps.title: Chapter 5
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'By June I ___ here for five years.'
steps.why: Future perfect continuous: duration up to a future point.

steps.title: Chapter 5
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which expresses the highest probability?
steps.why: Bound to is near-certainty.

steps.title: Chapter 5
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'I wouldn't be surprised if she ___ .'
steps.why: The past form marks distance from reality, not past time.

steps.title: Chapter 5
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Money you pay in yourself towards retirement is …
steps.why: A private pension.

steps.title: Chapter 6
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Somebody who is at their best late in the evening is …
steps.why: A night owl.

steps.title: Chapter 6
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Two things happening at once by chance is …
steps.why: Coincidence.

steps.title: Chapter 6
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which interruption is most polite?
options: If I could just come in there for a second …
steps.answer: If I could just come in there for a second …
steps.why: It asks permission and softens with just.

steps.title: Chapter 6
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Somebody interrupts you. Which reclaims your turn without hostility?
options: If I could just finish what I was saying …
Don't talk over me while I'm speaking.
I hadn't actually finished my point.
steps.answer: If I could just finish what I was saying …
steps.why: It names the interruption and returns to the point in one move.

steps.title: Chapter 6
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: A town loses the sun for six months. The usual cause is …
options: its latitude, like everywhere that far north
geography — a valley below a tall mountain
cloud that sits over it all winter
steps.answer: geography — a valley below a tall mountain
steps.why: Latitude alone would not do it; the mountain casts the shadow.

steps.title: Chapter 7
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'The prototype ___ tested at the moment.'
steps.why: Present continuous passive.

steps.title: Chapter 7
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: When is the passive the better choice?
options: When the agent is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
steps.answer: When the agent is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
steps.why: Formality alone is not the criterion.

steps.title: Chapter 7
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which expresses purpose rather than result?
options: The gym was installed, so fewer staff left the site.
The gym was installed so that staff would stay on site.
The gym was installed because staff kept leaving.
steps.answer: The gym was installed so that staff would stay on site.
steps.why: So that + a modal expresses intention.

steps.title: Chapter 7
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: They redesigned it in order to save weight.
They redesigned it for to save weight.
They redesigned it so as to save weight.
steps.answer: They redesigned it for to save weight.
steps.why: For to is not English.

steps.title: Chapter 7
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which disagrees while leaving the other person room to retreat?
options: Isn't that a bit old-fashioned, though?
steps.answer: Isn't that a bit old-fashioned, though?
steps.why: A hedged question states a position and preserves face.

steps.title: Chapter 8
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'She's very fussy ___ food.'
steps.why: Fussy about.

steps.title: Chapter 8
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'Quinoa is rich ___ protein.'
steps.why: Rich in.

steps.title: Chapter 8
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which sentence says that all the engineers design these systems?
options: The engineers who design these systems disagree.
The engineers, who design these systems, disagree.
Neither — the two mean the same.
steps.answer: The engineers, who design these systems, disagree.
steps.why: The commas make the clause non-defining.

steps.title: Chapter 8
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Generation labels, according to the level's reading, are …
options: useful about groups and useless about individuals
reliable only when researchers use them
steps.answer: useful about groups and useless about individuals
steps.why: Used carefully they describe what a group lived through.

steps.title: Chapter 8
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: 'It didn't live up to expectations.' The phrase measures the thing against …
options: what was promised or expected beforehand
steps.answer: what was promised or expected beforehand
steps.why: Live up to always implies a standard set in advance.

steps.title: Chapter 9
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: We used to have a garden.
We would sit in the garden every evening.
steps.why: Would covers repeated actions but not past states.

steps.title: Chapter 9
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'I'm used to ___ early.'
steps.why: The to in be used to is a preposition.

steps.title: Chapter 9
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'I look forward to ___ from you.'
steps.why: Same trap, same reason.

steps.title: Chapter 9
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which proposes rather than instructs?
options: What if we installed better lighting?
steps.answer: What if we installed better lighting?
steps.why: What if opens a proposal for the other person to weigh.

steps.title: Chapter 9
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'It might be worth ___ the wall first.'
steps.why: Worth takes the -ing form.

steps.title: Chapter 10
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'He admitted ___ carelessly.'
steps.why: Admit + -ing.

steps.title: Chapter 10
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'She assured me ___ be late.'
steps.why: Assure somebody that + clause.

steps.title: Chapter 10
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which reports a claim without endorsing it?
options: The ship was said to be carrying rats.
Rats were carried by the ship.
steps.answer: The ship was said to be carrying rats.
steps.why: Be said to attributes the claim elsewhere.

steps.title: Chapter 10
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: The way into a long, complex sentence is to find …
options: the main verb, then the subject
steps.answer: the main verb, then the subject
steps.why: Everything else hangs off the main clause.

steps.title: Chapter 10
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: 'It took six days, supposedly.' The speaker is …
steps.why: Supposedly marks the source.

steps.title: Chapter 11
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'Could you ___ at this a moment?'
steps.why: Look at = direct your eyes deliberately.

steps.title: Chapter 11
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: I watched the match last night.
I looked the match last night.
I saw at the match last night.
steps.answer: I watched the match last night.
steps.why: Watch for something that unfolds and holds attention.

steps.title: Chapter 11
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: You are not sure what the object is. Which is best?
options: They're in what looks like a rubber boat.
They're definitely in a rubber boat.
steps.answer: They're in what looks like a rubber boat.
steps.why: What looks like marks it as your interpretation.

steps.title: Chapter 11
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: You missed one phrase. Which repair is most efficient?
options: Sorry, what do you mean by 'in the foreground'?
Could you repeat all of that?
steps.answer: Sorry, what do you mean by 'in the foreground'?
steps.why: Naming the phrase means only that gets repaired.

steps.title: Chapter 11
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: The most reliable finding about humour is that a joke works when …
options: the audience does not see it coming
steps.answer: the audience does not see it coming
steps.why: Which is why a joke announced in advance cannot work.

steps.title: Chapter 12
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'If I had grown up alone, I ___ a different person now.'
steps.why: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

steps.title: Chapter 12
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: If she had applied, she might have got it.
If she would have applied, she might have got it.
Had she applied, she might have got it.
steps.answer: If she would have applied, she might have got it.
steps.why: Would never goes in the if clause.

steps.title: Chapter 12
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'She wishes she ___ something at the time.'
steps.why: A past regret takes the past perfect.

steps.title: Chapter 12
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
steps.why: The first element of a compound adjective stays singular.

steps.title: Chapter 12
steps.sub: Sixty questions, pass mark 70%. This is the assessment for the whole level.
steps.prompt: '___ , losing that job was a blessing in disguise.'
steps.why: The judgement was made afterwards.

steps.title: Урок пройден
steps.sub: Final Test · the whole B2 level
items: I have tested the level as a whole.
I have answered questions from all twelve chapters.
I can use the grammar of the level across contexts.
I know the vocabulary and functions of B2.
